summary: No. On BTC, ETH and SOL, price after a bullish or bearish divergence moved like price after a random candle on 1h, 4h and daily. This held for RSI divergence alone and for 2 or more oscillators agreeing. The one result that holds up is negative: on daily candles in uptrends, regular bullish divergence on 2+ oscillators did 7.9% worse than random entries after 20 days.

verdicts.text: Inside the luck band on 1h, 4h and daily, in uptrends and downtrends alike.
No better than random entries on 1h, 4h or daily. On daily it fired too rarely in each regime to be judged.
Inside the band on all three timeframes. On daily in downtrends it beat random, but only because of one stretch of signals between Apr 26 and Jun 22, 2022.
On 4h, price did worse than random after these signals. Only the signals on May 5–11, 2022, during the Terra collapse, produced that. Without them, chance.

verdicts.use: Regular bullish divergence on daily (2+ oscillators)
verdicts.text: Inside the band when both regimes are pooled. In uptrends alone, price did worse than random after 20 days, and that held without its strongest stretch and at 50 and 100 candles.

notes: Buying on any bullish divergence across 2+ oscillators on 1h gave 11,001 entries in 2,703 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.06% ahead of random entries, inside the luck band of -0.06% to 0.07%. The same setting fires about four times as often on 1h as on 4h, and it also lands inside the band on 4h and daily. Uptrends and downtrends show the same nothing.

On 1h, any bullish divergence fires about eight and a half times as often as RSI bullish divergence alone, and the stricter signal did no better. RSI divergence ended 0.01% behind random entries on 1h and 0.04% behind on 4h, both inside the band. Hidden bullish divergence on 1h beat random by 0.13% in downtrends, but five entries on Jan 13, 2023 carry that result. In uptrends it showed nothing.

Asking more oscillators to agree cuts the signal count hard: on 1h, 1+ oscillator fires about nine and a half times as often as 3+. It does not make the signals better. On 4h, regular bullish divergence on 3+ oscillators did 0.8% worse than random, just past the band's edge of -0.79%. Four entries on May 5–11, 2022, during the Terra collapse, account for that result, and without them it is chance.

On daily, regular bullish divergence on 1+ oscillator did 2.86% worse than random. That comes from 13 entries between Apr 23 and Jun 17, 2022, and without them it is chance. With 2+ oscillators the pooled daily result sits inside the band, but the regimes split it.

In uptrends, daily bullish divergence on 2+ oscillators did 7.9% worse than random after 20 days. That held without its strongest stretch and at 50 and 100 candles, and it rests on 30 moves, the fewest the test will judge. In downtrends it was 4.4% worse, but only because of signals between Apr 24 and May 28, 2022.

Shorting bearish divergence on 2+ oscillators landed inside the band on 1h, 4h and daily. On daily the two regimes differ: in downtrends the short beat random by 3.53%, and in uptrends it showed nothing. The downtrend result comes from 12 entries between Apr 26 and Jun 22, 2022, and without them it is chance.

On these pairs, a long DCA bot that starts on bullish divergence times its entries no better than one starting on a random candle, so the DCA orders and take profit do the work. If you keep divergence in a bot, use it as one filter beside your other conditions, not as the reason the bot opens a deal. On daily, consider leaving regular bullish divergence out as a start condition in uptrends, where price did worse than random after it. On a short bot, bearish divergence added nothing outside a single stretch of signals.
